title: Metal paint parity: contract-derived conformance scenes on every renderer, Apple code linted and built in CI, records synced, ToFix retired

The existing catalog group that exercises the touched `Area::REQUIRED` list and scene metadata: every new area has a scene, ids are unique kebab-case.
Lane A for the five `paint-contract-*` scenes: their bounds and behavior steps on `TestPlatform` (pixel steps are skipped there), plus the lane A listing test.
Lane C on this Mac's Metal renderer for the `paint-contract-*` scenes at scales 1 and 2 (`at_1x::paint_contract_*`, `at_2x::paint_contract_*`), one scene at a time, asserting the backend.
The existing fast-mode parity group that the lane A catalog list feeds, for the new scenes: each runs with fast mode on and off on `TestPlatform` and describes alike.
The existing fast-mode parity group that the lane C catalog list feeds, for the new scenes on Metal at scales 1 and 2: fast mode on and off render alike.

Lane B's `scenes.spec.ts` for the `paint-contract-*` scenes at DPR 1 (`@pr`) and DPR 2 (`@dpr2`) on WebGPU through the WGPU renderer's WGSL. Needs lane B's prerequisites (nightly `-Z build-std`, wasm-bindgen, Playwright Chromium). A WGSL change in PAR-4 adds a forced-WebGL2 run of the touched scenes and `dawn.spec.ts` (resolved when it happens).

CI's exact Clippy command on macOS. A whole-workspace run, justified because the CI step this sprint enables lints the whole macOS workspace: it must be green before the step lands.
The `runtime_shaders` build of `gpux-apple`, the command the new macOS CI step runs.
AgentX's workflow YAML checker (syntax errors and the duplicate keys GitHub rejects) over every workflow and the plan action. The script path is the installed AgentX skill's.

AgentX's memory audit from the Gpux root (structure, frontmatter, indexes, links). The script path is the installed AgentX skill's. No `inputs`: memory is metadata, so any change reruns it (it takes seconds).
The existing group that exercises the touched guard: `repository_layout.rs` without the `ToFix/` entry. Its stale-path scan reads every tracked live file, hence no `inputs`.
Clippy of the packages whose code changes, as CLAUDE.md runs it, on this Mac. Add `gpux-wgpu-renderer` or `gpux-macos` if PAR-4 changed their Rust code.
The iOS conformance host compiles with the new step (lane F runs it only nightly in CI): the features `gpux-testkit lane f` builds with, for the Simulator target.

The Android conformance host compiles with the new step (lane E runs it only nightly in CI), through cargo-ndk as `gpux-testkit lane e` builds it. Resolve the NDK environment (`ANDROID_NDK_HOME` or the testkit's pinned NDK) before final validation.
New group `tests/lane_c_paint_contract_scales.rs`: every `paint-contract-*` scene's probes on lane C's renderer (Metal here) at the mobile host scales 3 and 2.625.

The testkit groups that guard lane wiring: every conformance test target runs in a lane (`lane_coverage`), and the lane A/C plans and process splits list `ring_evenness` and `lane_c_paint_contract_scales` (`lane_jobs`, `cli`).

sprints.title: Paint-contract scenes, the ring-evenness step, and renderer parity on Metal and WebGPU

tasks.title: Add the ring-evenness pixel step and its test group
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
Implement STEP-1 per d-contract-scenes.

1. Read RayX's metric in `../RayX/tools-node/test_suite/rayx-border-antialiasing.spec.ts` (reference only; nothing in RayX changes).
2. Add the variant to `Step` in `crates/gpux_tests_conformance/src/scene.rs` with a doc comment, and include it wherever pixel steps are classified (`scene.rs`'s pixel-step test, `test_host.rs`, `app_host.rs`) and described (`host.rs`).
3. Put the measurement in `evaluate.rs` beside the other pixel evaluations, as a function of a captured RGBA frame, the element's device-pixel bounds, the scale and the limit, so the new test group can call it without a host. Expose what the test needs through the crate's existing public surface (`probe`/`evaluate` modules).
4. Write `tests/ring_evenness.rs`: synthesize anti-aliased rings (analytic coverage of a 1 px annulus, composited in encoded sRGB over `#0a0a0a`) at scales 1 and 2, centred on and off the pixel grid; a seeded beaded ring; an empty frame. Assert pass/fail and that the failure message carries the coefficient and the limit.

Keep the metric's constants (48 bins, reach `scale / 2 + 2`, backdrop at the centre) named and documented.

tasks.title: Add the inset-shadow, gradient, pattern and image-alpha scenes
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
Implement SCN-1 to SCN-4 and the catalog shape of SCN-6 per d-contract-scenes.

1. Add the encoded-sRGB `over` helper beside the scenes (`scenes/common.rs` or the new module) and use it for every composite expectation. OKLab expectations: use `gpux_color` and the renderers' stop preparation (`prepare_gradient_stop_color` in `crates/gpui/src/color.rs`, read-only here), so the scene states the contract rather than a measured value.
2. Add `paint-contract-inset-shadows`, `paint-contract-gradients`, `paint-contract-patterns` and `paint-contract-image-alpha` with `PIXEL_LANES`, scales `[1., 2.]`, `golden: false`, `Expect::Bounds` for each probed element, and the probes the criteria list. Place probes away from anti-aliased edges and pattern boundaries at both scales; comment each with the failure-mode value it rejects.
3. Add the new `Area` variants to `Area` and `Area::REQUIRED`, register the scenes in `CATALOG`, and list them in `tests/catalog/lane_a_scenes.rs` and `lane_c_scenes.rs`.
4. `RenderImage` frames are BGRA; keep the image's alpha straight.

Run the lane C check on Metal while writing the probes; a value that disagrees with the contract on Metal is t4's to resolve, not a reason to change the expectation.

tasks.title: Add the border-beading scene
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Implement SCN-5 per d-contract-scenes, using t1's step: three `rounded_full` 1 px rings (white, an accent blue, white at alpha 0.15) and a 4 px white box over `#0a0a0a`, sized like RayX's page so the ring circumference spans all 48 bins with several pixels each. Same catalog shape as t2 (prefix, lanes, scales, `golden: false`, area, both catalog lists). The limits are RayX's; do not tune them.

tasks.title: Run the scenes on Metal and WebGPU and fix the renderer that breaks the contract
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
Implement PAR-1 to PAR-4 per d-renderer-parity.

1. Run the lane C (Metal), lane B and lane D checks for the `paint-contract-*` scenes. Save raw output and failing frames (`artifacts-temp/testkit/c/` and Playwright reports) under `artifacts-temp/agentx/metal-paint-parity/`.
2. For each failure, decide from the contract whether the scene or a renderer is wrong (d-renderer-parity), then fix it at its source: `crates/gpui_apple/src/shaders.metal` and `metal_renderer.rs` for Metal, `crates/gpui_wgpu/src/shaders.wgsl` and `wgpu_renderer.rs` for WGPU. Expected suspects from the port's hand-off: inset shadows (`element_bounds`, `element_corner_radii`), OKLab stop conversion, pattern scaling, polychrome premultiplication, and Metal's hard-coded border gamma in `quad_fragment`.
3. Commit each fix separately, naming the scene that proves it; say in the body when the file is upstream-imported. A WGSL change also runs lane B's forced-WebGL2 route for the touched scenes and `dawn.spec.ts`; amend `check-lane-b-paint-contract` or add a focused check for it.
4. Record in the handoff (`advance --handoff`) every fix, or that none was needed, and the measured beading coefficients per ring, scale and lane: REC-1 needs them.

sprints.title: Clippy on macOS and the runtime_shaders build in CI

tasks.title: Fix the macOS Clippy findings and lint and build the Apple code in CI
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
Implement CI-1 to CI-3 per d-apple-ci. This sprint follows s1 so the workspace Clippy run also lints s1's code.

1. Run `check-macos-workspace-clippy`. Known finding: `crates/util/src/command/darwin/process.rs`, `tests::spawn` (`clippy::zombie_processes`, `clippy::disallowed_methods`); mark the helper `#[allow(clippy::disallowed_methods, clippy::zombie_processes)]` with a comment that `Process` reaps the pid, as `darwin.rs`'s tests do. Fix any other finding at its source, each with its own commit when it touches another crate.
2. In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `check` job: the Clippy step's `if:` becomes `runner.os != 'Linux'`; add `cargo check -p gpux-apple --features runtime_shaders` as a macOS-only step after `Check every target`, with a one-line comment.
3. Update `docs/testing.md`'s `ci.yml` paragraph to say Clippy runs on Windows and macOS, and `docs/ci.md` if it describes the `check` job's steps.
4. Run the three sprint checks. The hosted proof of CI-2 is the push's own CI run (`check (macos-15)` shows the Clippy and runtime_shaders steps); never dispatch an extra run.

sprints.title: Pattern probes that hold at every host scale (final review FINAL-F1)

tasks.title: Scale the patterns scene's geometry with the window and prove it at the mobile scales
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
Implement SCN-7 per d-pattern-host-scales.

1. Give `paint-contract-patterns` a view that reads `window.scale_factor()` at build and multiplies the checkerboard cell and the slash stripe and gap by it; re-place the probes in logical pixels with at least two logical pixels of margin at scales 1, 1.5, 2, 2.625 and 3 (check numerically against the WGSL pattern formulas), keeping the failure-mode comments.
2. Add `tests/lane_c_paint_contract_scales.rs`: every `paint-contract-*` scene through `TestHost::pixels().probes_only()` at scales 3 and 2.625, asserting the backend when `GPUX_EXPECT_BACKEND` is set.
3. Rerun lanes A, C (Metal), B (WebGPU) and D for the paint-contract scenes.
4. Wire the new group into lane C (`LANE_C_GROUPS`, `LANE_C_WEIGHTS` in `tools/testkit/src/lanes.rs`) and `ring_evenness` (STEP-1's group, unwired since s1) into lane A's groups, so CI runs them; update the testkit tests that list the groups and `docs/testing.md` (sprint review S4-F1).
